title: Console minimal data contract & fallback spec for compact insights
creator: Marco Ruiz
summary: Define a narrow, backwards-compatible data contract and graceful fallback behavior for Compact Insights cards (route-level cost rollups, sampling-enabled traces, trimmed metric set) so we can ship a stable MVP surface with clear acceptance criteria and operational runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Compact Insights card uses a reduced data contract: {route, latency_p50, latency_p95, token_cost, trace_sample_id} and renders without blocking on optional fields
If route-level cost rollups are delayed or missing, UI shows stale totals with a clear warning and an ETA link to status page
Trace linking works for sampled traces: clicking trace_sample_id opens trace view for that sample; if trace unavailable, fallback links to request-level logs
Cost breakdown shows aggregated buckets (compute, embeddings, infra) rather than per-token micro-details for MVP to limit ingestion volume
Backend exposes a compatibility header indicating contract version; console falls back to v1 rendering when header absent
End-to-end latency target for card render under typical load: <= 500ms median, <= 1200ms p95 when using cache; measured in canary rollout
Feature flag guard exists (feature.console.compact_insights_v1) and can be toggled per-org for staged rollout
Acceptance verified by product QA checklist and automated E2E test that asserts front-end gracefully handles missing optional fields
decisions: Trimmed metric set chosen to reduce ingestion: removed per-route token-by-token delta in favor of periodic rollup (5m cadence)
Sampled tracing only: retain 1 in 200 requests for trace linkage in MVP to balance cost vs debugability
Fallback UX: prefer showing stale data with visible timestamp + 'Refresh & ETA' link rather than hiding the card
Use compatibility header approach to avoid server-side branching for older control-plane integrations
tradeoffs_and_rationale: Reduced observability fidelity (sampling + rollups) increases mean time to debug for some incidents but cuts ingestion cost by estimated 60% for MVP
Fallback visible warning increases user noise but avoids silent failures and reduces support load
Contract simplicity speeds implementation across hosted/dedicated/private but requires clear migration docs for customers who relied on previous granular fields
rollout_plan: Week 0: Merge API + schema PR behind compatibility header and feature flag; basic unit tests
Week 1: Canary to 5% of orgs (internal + trusted customers) with telemetry hooks for latency, error rate, and data completeness
Week 2: Expand to 25% after canary review; run targeted internal SLA tests for p95 render latency
Week 3: Full rollout if no regressions and SLAs met; otherwise iterate on batching and cache TTLs
Rollback criteria: +30% increase in p95 render latency, >2% error surface, or critical customer report within canary cohort
qa_checks: Automated E2E: simulate missing optional fields and assert UI renders and 'stale' banner appears
Load test: validate p95 under simulated 10k concurrent routes with rollups enabled
Compatibility test: send both v1 and missing header requests and assert front-end uses fallback rendering
Manual UX review: product and design validate the fallback messaging for clarity and next steps
Security smoke: ensure no sensitive PII appears in rollup payloads and KMS usage confirmed for private deployments
monitoring_and_alerting: PagerDuty: trigger if p95 render latency > 1.5s for >10 minutes during rollout window
SLO: 99% successful card renders during business hours for canary orgs
Audit: log schema version mismatch events to internal compliance stream
notes_and_links: Design feedback summary (01/18): prefer explicit ETA to obscure spinner; action: add ETA field to PRD
Eng implementation notes (01/24): will implement rollup writer as incremental job; ENG-98421 tracks runtime batching changes
Customer feedback: finance team asked for compute/embed splits; included as aggregated buckets rather than per-token line items
Related doc: incident learnings on trace sampling tradeoffs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/IR/Trace+Sampling+Postmortem
